title: The seed rides home
question: Does the pip read as a seed the ant is carrying, and then putting down, rather than just an ant walking around?
context_md:
A2 -- Brief A2 of `Reports/evolution-lab-ecology-design-2026-09-10.md`: when a fruit's seed survives the bite (A1, PR #301), it now rides in the ant's crop instead of standing where it was bitten, and is put down as a live organism -- same genome, same lineage -- wherever the ant next drops a load.

`played_bed`, seed 2, `scenario=played_bed frames=120000`. Two real deliveries land inside this window, at frames 49134 (x=329,y=155, carried 36 frames) and 49340 (x=324,y=158, carried 175 frames) -- the clip is centred between them, zoom 5x (102x64 world cells visible). Nothing is staged; this is a real run, real ants, real bites.

**Read `PAUSED -- NOTHING IS TICKING` as a harness artifact, not a bug.** `labgif` drives frames through `tick_for_harness` rather than the play/pause dial, so the corner HUD reads PAUSED the whole time even though the box is genuinely running underneath it -- the frame counter in the same corner is the real clock.

**Honest reading of the numbers, not just the picture**: across this seed, 6 seeds were carried and 4 delivered (2 still mid-transit when the run ended); of the 4 delivered, 2 were later re-bitten and 1 decayed before germinating. None of the 6 has germinated into a standing plant by frame 120,000 in this run, so `plants_from_pip_near_nest` reads 0 here -- the mechanism fires and conserves matter correctly (verified by five unit tests, each watched red before green), but this window is too short to show a seed becoming a plant. That is a finding about this bed's bite rate and germination timing, not a defect in the ride-home mechanism -- see the PR body for the full per-seed table.
